findings.title: Design cannot reach the planned power
findings.why_it_matters: With too few units a real effect of the planned size is likely to be missed, and a result of no significant difference then says little. If the target effect cannot exist at all, for example a rate above 1 after the relative lift, no sample size can reach it.
findings.remediation: Run for the required days, bring in more eligible units, accept the larger minimum detectable effect the evidence reports, or choose a target effect that can exist.
references: Kohavi, Tang, Xu. Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments. Cambridge University Press, 2020.

findings.title: No stopping rule declared
findings.why_it_matters: Looking at results repeatedly and stopping when they look significant pushes the false-positive rate of a fixed-horizon test well above the chosen alpha. Without a declared rule, a planned stop cannot be told from a peek.
findings.remediation: Set procedure.stopping_rule to fixed_horizon (analyse once, at the planned end) or to sequential (and use a test designed for repeated looks).
references: Johari, Koomen, Pekelis, Walsh. Peeking at A/B Tests: Why It Matters, and What to Do About It. KDD 2017.
Kohavi, Tang, Xu. Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments. Cambridge University Press, 2020.

findings.title: Interference between units is possible
findings.why_it_matters: If one player's treatment can change another's behaviour, as with social or multiplayer features, units are not independent and the measured effect can be biased.
findings.remediation: Randomize at a level that contains the interaction (clusters of players), or set population.interference to none_expected and record why.
references: Kohavi, Tang, Xu. Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments. Cambridge University Press, 2020.

findings.title: No pre-period covariate declared
findings.why_it_matters: A covariate measured before the experiment lets the analysis remove variance that has nothing to do with the treatment (CUPED), which can shorten the test or sharpen the estimate.
findings.remediation: Declare design.pre_period_covariate, for example the primary metric measured for each unit before exposure.
references: Deng, Xu, Kohavi, Walker. Improving the Sensitivity of Online Controlled Experiments by Utilizing Pre-Experiment Data. WSDM 2013.

findings.title: No sample-ratio-mismatch check scheduled
findings.why_it_matters: When arm counts depart from the registered allocation, assignment or logging is broken and the comparison is invalid. The mismatch is found only if someone checks.
findings.remediation: Set procedure.srm_check_cadence to daily (recommended) or weekly, and act on a mismatch before reading any result.
references: Fabijan et al. Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments. KDD 2019.
Kohavi, Tang, Xu. Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments. Cambridge University Press, 2020.

findings.title: The cohort check of the results review would not run on this plan
findings.why_it_matters: After the experiment, the cohort check of the results review (RES-007) compares each arm's effect between cohorts of first exposure, to find an effect that differs between the players who joined in different weeks (a launch, a promotion, a change in who is acquired). It does not test for novelty or adaptation: DES-003 is the rule for those. It works in blocks of 7 days, or of 14 days on a plan of 42 days or more, and the gates above are its own, applied to the plan's expected numbers. Real arrivals are less even than expected numbers, so a plan that only just passes still fails in many runs; this rule names the plans that fail even in the best case. When the check cannot run, the results review says so in a RES-007 warning and its verdict is caution, not clear. This is a forecast from the plan, not a finding about the data.
findings.remediation: If an effect that differs between the weeks players joined could matter for this change, plan at least 21 days (42 days or more allows blocks of 14 days, which need fewer players a week), bring in more eligible units each day or give the smaller arm a larger share, keep the arms within 9 to 1, and randomise and analyse in the same independent unit (player, user or device). The evidence gives the units a day that pass with even arrivals; allow more, because arrivals vary (design section 21.6: spiky arrivals need 1.5 to 3 times as much). Otherwise accept that the cohort check will not run: the other results checks are not affected.

findings.title: Bucketing salt not declared
findings.why_it_matters: Assignment hashes the unit ID with a salt. Reusing one salt across experiments gives them the same bucket boundaries, which can carry one experiment's effect into the next.
findings.remediation: Set procedure.bucketing_salt to a value unique to this experiment, for example its id.
references: Kohavi, Deng, Frasca, Longbotham, Walker, Xu. Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: Five Puzzling Outcomes Explained. KDD 2012.
